Pegasus 1.6 turns first-person video into robotics training data

TwelveLabs adds action segmentation, descriptions and clip assessment to support behavioral datasets, without replacing tactile sensors or robot control.

The Robot Report ↗6 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2Videos 1

Understanding the operator’s viewpoint

TwelveLabs released Pegasus 1.6 on October 6 with support for video captured from the viewpoint of the person or machine doing a task, such as assembly, cooking or robot teleoperation. It also improves entity recognition and handles still images through the same API as video. The company does not require a proprietary capture camera.

Preparing reviewable datasets

Supported workflows include timed action labels, detailed captions, quality scoring, search for rare events or duplicate clips, and flagging faces, bystanders or sensitive data. These tools help teams organize raw footage for review and training selection. Flagging is an aid to review; it does not itself establish consent or guarantee compliance in every situation.

Video analysis has a defined role

Pegasus identifies visible behavior, such as what each hand is doing and how a scene changes, for teams to combine with their own sensor data. It does not replace tactile or actuator-level sensing or make a robot execute a task simply by reading footage. The reviewed announcement provides no independent, across-task measurement of improved robot success rates.
